who.h2: Training and certification: who does what
who.intro: A course gives you training. It does not certify you. Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A (2024 edition) your employer certifies you under its written practice, and ASNT also runs central certification. Each part is separate:

columns.h3: What the Atlantis course gives you
items: Documented training hours for the method and level, recorded per person
Theory: self-paced material plus live online sessions with replays
Practice in the Practical NDT simulator
Supervised hands-on practical at your employer's facility, on its own equipment and parts
A training record that you and your employer can keep on file for audits

columns.h3: What your employer does under SNT-TC-1A
items: Keeps a written practice that sets the training, experience and examination requirements
Gives the general, specific and practical examinations
Carries out the vision examination (near-vision acuity and color contrast)
Logs and verifies your experience in the method
Certifies you. That certification belongs to the employer and does not move with you to a new job
ASNT NDT Level II: ASNT administers a computer-based general exam and specific exams, in MT, PT, RT, UT and VT
ASNT states that employers are responsible for carrying out the visual acuity, practical and any job-specific exams
ASNT NDT Level III: the Basic exam plus at least one method exam, with documented NDT experience
ASNT certifications are renewed every five years
link: ASNT NDT Level II requirements on certification.asnt.org

who.closing: Completing a course finishes the training part only. Experience, examinations and certification still have to be completed and documented.

practical.intro: There are no fixed course dates. Enrollment is open all year.
steps: Course starts run in the first week of each month, and you can enroll at other times too. There are no dated cohorts to wait for.
Work through the self-paced material, join the live online sessions or watch the replays, and ask the Level III when something is unclear.
Use the Practical NDT simulator to rehearse the method before you touch real parts.
An ASNT Level III supervises practical training at your employer's facility, on its own equipment and parts. Atlantis has no classroom, partner site or public venue for practicals.
Your employer gives the practical examination under its written practice. An outside Level III, including Atlantis, can administer it for the employer.

items: Instrument set-up
Calibration
Scanning discipline
Coverage of the area to be examined
Following procedure steps in order
The feel of couplant and probe pressure
Real signal noise
Real surface condition, access and geometry on actual parts

practical.note: Simulator time counts as training. It does not count as industrial experience hours unless a certification body or your employer's written practice explicitly allows it.

methodCommon.checksH2: What the employer's {short} practical exam checks
methodCommon.checksIntro: Your employer's written practice and procedure set the specimens and pass criteria. In general the practical examination checks that you can:

UT.name: ultrasonic testing
topics: Principles: wave modes, velocity, wavelength, acoustic impedance, refraction, Snell's law and mode conversion
Equipment: flaw detectors, straight-beam, angle-beam and dual-element transducers, wedges and couplants
Calibration and standardization on reference blocks: range, sensitivity, DAC and TCG
Techniques: straight-beam and angle-beam contact testing, weld scanning and thickness measurement
Interpretation and evaluation: telling geometry from relevant indications, then locating and sizing reflectors
Codes and procedures: working to a written procedure, ASME Section V and the acceptance criteria of the referencing code
Reporting: recording indications, coverage and calibration data so a reviewer can follow them
Safety: site access, surface preparation and working around live plant
checks: Calibrate range and sensitivity on the specified reference block and re-check calibration when the procedure requires
Scan the required volume with the right angles, directions and overlap, so coverage is complete
Detect, locate and size the reflectors in a practical specimen and evaluate them against the procedure's acceptance criteria
Record the results and calibration data on a traceable report

UT.subject: UT%20training

RT.name: radiographic testing
topics: Radiation physics: X-ray and gamma sources, attenuation, half-value layer and the inverse square law
Radiation safety: dose, shielding, survey meters and controlled areas (radiation safety licensing is separate from NDT certification)
Recording media: film, computed radiography plates and digital detectors
Exposure technique: source-to-film distance, geometric unsharpness, single-wall and double-wall techniques
Image quality: density, contrast and image quality indicators (IQIs) and their placement
Processing and viewing conditions
Interpretation and evaluation: weld and casting discontinuities, artifacts and acceptance criteria
Codes and procedures: ASME Section V and the referencing construction code
Reporting
checks: Set up an exposure to the written technique, including source-to-film distance and IQI selection and placement
Show that the image meets the required quality and IQI sensitivity
Interpret a set of radiographs, separate discontinuities from artifacts and apply the acceptance criteria
Work within the radiation safety rules and record the results
l3Prep: ASNT Level III RT exam prep
RT.subject: RT%20training

MT.name: magnetic particle testing
topics: Magnetism: magnetic fields, permeability and flux leakage at a discontinuity
Magnetization methods: yokes, prods, coils, central conductors and head shots; circular and longitudinal fields
Current types (AC, half-wave and full-wave rectified) and what each one finds
Media: dry powder and wet visible or fluorescent particles, and UV-A lighting for fluorescent work
Field verification with field indicators and shims
Technique: surface preparation, two perpendicular directions, coverage and overlap
Interpretation and evaluation: relevant and non-relevant indications against acceptance criteria
Demagnetization and post-cleaning
Codes and procedures: ASME Section V and ASTM practices for MT
Safety: electrical hazards, UV-A exposure and handling of particle baths
checks: Prepare the surface and set up the magnetizing technique the procedure specifies
Verify field direction and adequacy, examining in two perpendicular directions
Apply particles correctly, cover the whole area and find the indications on the specimen
Evaluate relevant and non-relevant indications, demagnetize where required and record the results
l3Prep: ASNT Level III MT exam prep
MT.subject: MT%20training

PT.name: penetrant testing
topics: Principles: capillary action and how flaw geometry governs penetration
Penetrant systems: visible and fluorescent, sensitivity levels and removal methods (water-washable, post-emulsifiable, solvent-removable)
Surface preparation and pre-cleaning
Dwell time and temperature limits
Removing excess penetrant without over-washing
Developers: forms and application
Viewing conditions: visible light, UV-A intensity and dark adaptation
Interpretation and evaluation: relevant, non-relevant and false indications against acceptance criteria
Process controls and system checks; codes and procedures (ASME Section V and ASTM practices for PT)
Safety: chemical handling, ventilation and UV-A exposure
checks: Clean and prepare the specimen and apply penetrant for the dwell time the procedure sets
Remove excess penetrant without over-washing and apply an even coat of developer
Inspect under the required lighting, including UV-A intensity and dark adaptation for fluorescent work
Find and evaluate the indications against the acceptance criteria and record them
l3Prep: ASNT Level III PT exam prep
PT.subject: PT%20training

VT.name: visual testing
topics: Vision and lighting: acuity, light at the surface, viewing angle and distance
Direct and remote visual examination: mirrors, magnifiers, borescopes and video probes
Measuring tools: weld gauges, rulers, calipers and pit gauges
Materials and processes: how welding, casting, forging and service conditions produce discontinuities
Discontinuities: undercut, porosity, cracks, overlap and weld profile; corrosion and erosion in service
Codes and acceptance criteria: the referencing construction or in-service inspection code
Procedures and reporting
Safety: access and site hazards
checks: Confirm that lighting and viewing conditions meet the procedure before examining
Examine the specimen systematically for full coverage, directly or with remote equipment
Measure features such as undercut depth, weld size and reinforcement with the correct gauges
Record what is present and evaluate it against the stated acceptance criteria
l3Prep: ASNT Level III VT exam prep
VT.subject: VT%20training

ET.name: eddy current testing
topics: Principles: electromagnetic induction, eddy current flow and standard depth of penetration
Material and set-up variables: conductivity, permeability, lift-off and fill factor
The impedance plane display and phase analysis
Probes and coils: surface, bobbin and encircling coils; absolute and differential
Frequency selection
Reference standards and calibration
Applications: surface crack detection, tubing, conductivity and coating thickness
Interpretation and evaluation of signals against the procedure's criteria
Codes and procedures: ASME Section V and the referencing standard
Reporting
checks: Select the probe and frequency the procedure calls for and calibrate on the reference standard
Set up the display (gain and phase rotation) so lift-off and flaw signals separate as required
Scan the specimen with the required coverage and detect the reference or flaw signals
Evaluate and record the indications against the procedure's criteria
